hook.text: You found a great Airbnb host. Next time, why not book directly and skip the platform fee?

buildup.text: Disintermediation is when users cut out the platform and deal directly. It's every platform's nightmare.

discovery.text: Platforms fight back with insurance, payment protection, and dispute resolution you can't get going direct.

twist.text: Thumbtack and Fiverr make it easy to find a provider but hard to communicate outside the platform.

climax.text: If a platform doesn't add ongoing value, users will eventually bypass it. Matching alone isn't enough.

punchline.text: Match, then add value forever. Or get cut out.

quiz.question: What is platform disintermediation?
options: Users bypassing the platform to deal directly

details.summary: Platform disintermediation occurs when a platform eliminates traditional middlemen by connecting producers and consumers directly. Amazon removing retail stores, Airbnb bypassing hotels, and Spotify replacing record stores all disintermediated established distribution channels.
details.whyItMatters: Disintermediation creates enormous value by reducing transaction costs, but it also destroys incumbents and entire industries. Understanding when platforms disintermediate helps predict which industries face disruption.
takeaways: Platforms bypass incumbents by directly connecting supply and demand
Disintermediation reduces costs but destroys traditional intermediary businesses
New intermediation often replaces old: platforms become the new middlemen

faq.question: Which industries are most vulnerable to platform disintermediation?
faq.answer: Industries with expensive intermediaries adding limited value, fragmented supply, and information asymmetry. Real estate, financial advisory, insurance brokerage, and education are all seeing platform disintermediation compress traditional distribution margins.

faq.question: Do platforms always eliminate middlemen permanently?
faq.answer: Not always. Platforms often become new intermediaries themselves, sometimes charging higher total fees than the middlemen they replaced. Amazon takes up to 50% of seller revenue through fees. Re-intermediation through platforms is a common pattern in digital markets.
